title: Flavor Flux Correlators, Forward-Backward Asymmetries, and Anomalies
summary: Flavor plays a crucial role in the structure of the Standard Model. As such, many important collider physics measurements incorporate the flavor information of detected hadrons. Recent progress in the study of energy correlators has enabled collider physics measurements of energy flux to be reformulated as operator statements. In this Letter, we introduce flavor flux correlators, which measure the angular distribution and correlations of flavor quantum numbers. We emphasize a unique feature of heavy flavor flux correlators as compared to correlators of other charges, namely the $b$ and $c$ flavor quantum numbers are gapped at the heavy quark mass scale, making them a particularly clean perturbative observables, with $\mathcal{O}(Λ_{\text{QCD}}/m_Q)$ suppressed non-perturbative power corrections. As an application, we reformulate the heavy quark forward-backward asymmetry as a macroscopic consequence of a mixed electroweak anomaly of the heavy-quark flavor current. Using the relation to the anomaly, we compute the flavor flux correlator analytically at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order and verify using parton shower simulations that non-perturbative corrections are suppressed, as expected from the gapped nature of the heavy flavor quantum numbers. Flavor flux correlators can be measured using archival electron-positron collision data, as well as at Belle II and future colliders.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces 'flavor flux correlators'—a new class of collider observables that measure angular correlations of flavor quantum numbers (e.g., b/c quarks), leveraging their gapped nature at the heavy-quark mass scale to ensure clean perturbative calculability with suppressed Λ_QCD/m_Q non-perturbative corrections. As a key application, it reformulates the heavy-quark forward-backward asymmetry as arising from a mixed electroweak anomaly of the flavor current, computes the corresponding correlator analytically at N³LO, and validates suppression of non-perturbative effects via parton shower simulations.
AI.motivation: To develop theoretically clean, experimentally accessible observables sensitive to flavor dynamics in collider physics—specifically exploiting the gapped nature of heavy-flavor quantum numbers (b/c) to suppress non-perturbative QCD effects and enable high-precision perturbative predictions.
AI.method: Introduces flavor flux correlators as angular correlation functions of flavor currents; uses anomaly matching and effective field theory techniques to relate the heavy-quark forward-backward asymmetry to a mixed electroweak anomaly; performs analytic N³LO QCD calculation of the flavor flux correlator; validates power-suppression of non-perturbative corrections using parton shower Monte Carlo simulations (e.g., Pythia).
AI.result: Derives the first analytic N³LO prediction for a heavy-flavor flux correlator; demonstrates numerically that Λ_QCD/m_Q power corrections are strongly suppressed (~1% level), confirming theoretical cleanliness; shows experimental feasibility using e⁺e⁻ data (e.g., LEP, Belle II).
AI.conclusion: Flavor flux correlators provide a novel, perturbatively robust framework for precision flavor physics at colliders; their gapped nature makes them uniquely suitable for high-order calculations and anomaly-driven interpretations, opening avenues for probing electroweak and QCD dynamics through flavor angular correlations.

title: Predictive Non-Minimal SU(5) GUT
comment: 14 pages + references, 3 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: Breaking of $SU(5)$ down to the Standard Model gauge group can be implemented by any non-trivial self-conjugate scalar representation with a suitable vacuum expectation value. The Georgi-Glashow model accomplishes this breaking with a 24-dimensional representation. That choice, although the most economical one, fails to unify the gauge coupling constants. Moreover, subsequent breaking of the Standard Model down to $SU(3) \times U(1)_\mathrm{em}$ with a $5$-dimensional representation fails to simultaneously provide viable masses for the down-type quarks and the charged leptons. We show that the substitution of the $24$-dimensional representation with a $75$-dimensional representation fixes the gauge coupling unification issue outrightly. We furthermore pin down, by computing the full mass spectrum of the multiplets in $75$-dimensional representation, the range of the unification scale $m_{\rm GUT}$ to be $10^{15}\,\text{GeV} \lesssim m_{\rm GUT} \lesssim 10^{16}\,\text{GeV}$. This unification window is partially excluded by Super-Kamiokande data and will be experimentally accessible at Hyper-Kamiokande. The second issue with the Georgi-Glashow model can be addressed, for example, with vectorlike fermions. The $24$-dimensional scenario admits three different types of vectorlike fermions that can properly account for the mismatch between the down-type quark and the charged lepton masses. The $75$-dimensional scenario, on the other hand, offers enhanced predictivity by allowing only a unique vectorlike addition of $10_F + \overline{10}_F$ that restores realistic charged fermion masses and modestly pushes the upper limit on the unification scale to $m_{\rm GUT} \lesssim 3\times10^{16}\,\text{GeV}$. The proposed framework with $75$-dimensional scalar representation can thus serve as a phenomenologically viable alternative to the standard Georgi-Glashow symmetry breaking paradigm.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes replacing the 24-dimensional Higgs representation in SU(5) Grand Unified Theory (GUT) with a 75-dimensional one to resolve gauge coupling unification and fermion mass issues; it predicts a GUT scale of 10^15–3×10^16 GeV, testable at Hyper-Kamiokande.
AI.motivation: The standard Georgi-Glashow SU(5) model fails to unify gauge couplings and cannot simultaneously generate realistic down-type quark and charged lepton masses using minimal Higgs representations.
AI.method: Analysis of SU(5) symmetry breaking via vacuum expectation values of self-conjugate scalar representations (24 vs. 75); computation of full mass spectrum of the 75-plet; evaluation of renormalization group evolution of gauge couplings; incorporation of vectorlike fermions (10_F + 10̅_F) to fix fermion mass relations.
AI.result: The 75-dimensional representation restores precise gauge coupling unification; constrains m_GUT ∈ [10^15, 10^16] GeV (extended to ~3×10^16 GeV with vectorlike fermions); uniquely permits only the 10_F + 10̅_F vectorlike extension for viable fermion masses.
AI.conclusion: The 75-plet SU(5) GUT provides a phenomenologically viable, predictive alternative to the Georgi-Glashow model, with testable implications for proton decay experiments.

title: Direct detection of right-handed fermionic dark matter: electron-recoil measurements in Xe atoms
summary: We present theoretical estimations of the event rates for the interaction between a right-handed fermionic dark matter with an electron bound to a xenon atom. Motivated by recent astrophysical and cosmological constraints on a fermionic dark matter candidate in the sub-MeV mass range, we study such an interaction through an effective electromagnetic channel where the output consists of standard-model particles. This mechanism allows right-handed neutral dark matter fermions to couple with standard-model particles with the interchange of $W^{\pm}$ or $Z$ bosons, without the need to add extra fields. We generalize and extend previous results on this type of channels, by including for the ionization form factor arising from the interaction of the fermionic candidate with bound electrons. In addition, we compute the sensitivity curves for different direct detection experiments in such a challenging light particle mass range.

AI.tldr: This paper theoretically estimates event rates for sub-MeV right-handed fermionic dark matter interacting with bound electrons in xenon via an effective electromagnetic channel involving W±/Z boson exchange, incorporating ionization form factors and deriving experimental sensitivity curves.
AI.motivation: Recent astrophysical and cosmological constraints on sub-MeV fermionic dark matter motivate investigation of its direct detection via novel electromagnetic-like interactions without introducing new fields.
AI.method: Theoretical calculation of event rates using an effective operator framework where right-handed neutral fermionic DM couples to SM particles via W±/Z exchange; inclusion of atomic ionization form factor for electron binding effects in xenon; derivation of expected sensitivity curves for current and future direct detection experiments.
AI.result: Updated event rate predictions and projected sensitivity limits for sub-MeV right-handed fermionic DM in xenon-based detectors, extending prior work by incorporating realistic atomic physics (ionization form factor) and benchmarking against experimental capabilities.
AI.conclusion: The proposed W±/Z-mediated electromagnetic channel is viable for detecting light right-handed fermionic DM, and inclusion of the ionization form factor significantly impacts predicted rates and experimental reach in the sub-MeV mass regime.

title: A Unified Numerical Study of Axion Stars: From the Nonrelativistic Regime to General Relativity
summary: Axion-star mass-radius relations are commonly computed using different orders of relativistic approximation, making it important to determine where these descriptions remain reliable. We perform a unified numerical comparison of axion-star ground-state configurations in the Newtonian Schrödinger-Poisson description, first- and second-order relativistic effective field theories, and the full Einstein-Klein-Gordon system for a real scalar field. Using the same attractive quartic self-interaction in all four descriptions, we scan $|\widetildeλ|=(M_{\rm Pl}/f_a)^2$ and determine the maximum masses and corresponding enclosed-mass radii. All descriptions recover the common large-$|\widetildeλ|$ dilute-star scaling, while substantial differences appear at weak and moderate coupling. The relativistic EFTs interpolate systematically between the Newtonian and full-GR results. For part of the maximum-mass sequence where $\max|φ|/f_a=O(1)$, we test the temporal-harmonic and potential truncations explicitly in full GR. The higher-harmonic expansion shows rapid convergence, while restoring the complete single-cosine potential changes the maximum mass only at the percent level and $R_{95}$ at the several-percent level. Together with the systematic convergence of the relativistic EFT descriptions toward full GR, these results show that the large weak-coupling departure from the Schrödinger-Poisson prediction reflects the breakdown of the nonrelativistic structural description. Our results provide a systematic benchmark for determining when Newtonian, relativistically corrected, or fully general-relativistic descriptions are required for axion-star structure. The numerical implementation used in this work is available in the Axion Star Solvers repository at https://github.com/Parisa-Arabameri/AxionStar.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically compares axion-star mass-radius relations across four theoretical frameworks—Newtonian Schrödinger-Poisson, first- and second-order relativistic EFTs, and full Einstein-Klein-Gordon—with identical quartic self-interaction. It shows relativistic EFTs systematically bridge Newtonian and full-GR results; higher harmonics converge rapidly in full GR, and the single-cosine potential approximation introduces only O(1%) errors in maximum mass. The study establishes quantitative benchmarks for choosing appropriate gravity regimes in axion-star modeling.
AI.motivation: To determine the validity domain of commonly used approximations (Newtonian SP, relativistic EFTs) for axion-star structure by benchmarking against full general-relativistic (Einstein-Klein-Gordon) solutions, especially where nonrelativistic assumptions break down (e.g., when |φ|/fa ~ O(1)).
AI.method: Unified numerical computation of ground-state axion-star configurations across four frameworks: (i) Newtonian Schrödinger-Poisson, (ii) first-order relativistic EFT, (iii) second-order relativistic EFT, and (iv) full Einstein-Klein-Gordon for a real scalar field—all with identical attractive quartic self-interaction. Scans over coupling |λ̃| = (M_Pl/fa)²; computes maximum masses and enclosed-mass radii (e.g., R₉₅). In full GR, explicitly tests temporal-harmonic truncation and potential truncation (single-cosine vs. full cosine).
AI.result: All frameworks recover dilute-star scaling at large |λ̃|; significant deviations emerge at weak/moderate coupling. Relativistic EFTs interpolate systematically between Newtonian and full-GR results. In full GR, higher-harmonic expansion converges rapidly; restoring full cosine potential alters maximum mass by ~1% and R₉₅ by several percent. The Newtonian breakdown coincides with |φ|/fa ~ O(1), confirming its structural inadequacy in that regime.
AI.conclusion: The observed large deviations from Schrödinger-Poisson predictions at weak coupling are due to intrinsic failure of the nonrelativistic structural description—not numerical or modeling artifacts. Relativistic EFTs provide quantitatively reliable, systematically improvable approximations. This work delivers concrete, parameter-dependent criteria for selecting Newtonian, relativistically corrected, or full-GR treatments in axion-star astrophysics and phenomenology.

title: Certified robustness of quantum spin textures under magnetic-field perturbations
summary: How much can a magnetic field change before a quantum spin texture loses its skyrmion charge? We address this question by combining the geometry of local spin expectation values with spectral perturbation theory. For a triangulated spin-$s$ texture, we determine the smallest change in its local moments that makes the reconstructed topological charge ill-defined, allowing unequal error bounds and fixed boundary moments. This geometric threshold yields explicit bounds on magnetic-field perturbations that preserve the ground-state charge, with $1/N$ scaling when the gap and geometric margin have positive limits. We apply the bounds to finite spin-$1/2$ systems with exchange and Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions. In a rigorously verified seven-spin example, the charge changes at a single certified field while the excitation gap and all local spin polarizations remain bounded away from zero; at such a crossing the geometric margin and the field certificate vanish linearly. The results provide quantitative certificates of texture stability and clarify the limitations of spectral-gap protection.

AI.tldr: This paper derives geometric and spectral bounds on magnetic-field perturbations that preserve the topological skyrmion charge of quantum spin textures, showing that charge instability can occur even when the excitation gap and local polarizations remain nonzero—highlighting limitations of gap-based stability arguments.
AI.motivation: To quantify how much a magnetic field can be varied before a quantum spin texture loses its well-defined skyrmion (topological) charge—addressing a fundamental question about robustness of topological order in finite quantum magnets.
AI.method: Combines differential geometry of local spin expectation values on a triangulated lattice with spectral perturbation theory; computes the minimal perturbation to local moments that renders the reconstructed topological charge ill-defined, under constraints of fixed boundary moments and unequal error bounds.
AI.result: Derives explicit, computable bounds on magnetic-field changes preserving ground-state skyrmion charge; shows 1/N scaling when gap and geometric margin converge to positive limits; demonstrates in a rigorously verified 7-spin model that charge change occurs at a certified field where geometric margin vanishes linearly—even while gap and all local spin polarizations stay bounded away from zero.
AI.conclusion: Topological charge stability cannot be guaranteed solely by a nonzero spectral gap or local polarization; geometric margins are essential and quantifiable certificates—revealing intrinsic limitations of spectral-gap protection in finite interacting spin systems.

title: Survey of Novel Deep Learning Architectures for Denoising Gravitational-wave Signals
comment: Submitted to "Machine Learning: Science and Technology", 52 pages, 35 Figures, 8 Tables
summary: Gravitational-wave denoising must handle the full diversity of spinning, precessing binaries, since the recovered waveform underpins parameter estimation, tests of general relativity, and population studies. Matched filtering achieves this at a cost that becomes prohibitive as next-generation detectors push event rates higher; deep learning offers real-time reconstruction, but current methods are developed on narrow parameter spaces, precluding principled comparison and reliable deployment. We present the first controlled comparison of five neural-network architectures for gravitational-wave denoising, trained identically across the full astrophysically-motivated spinning binary-black-hole parameter space. A unifying principle emerges: matching network structure to the spectral anatomy of a coalescence -- inspiral, merger, ringdown -- outperforms brute-force model scaling. Our Multi-Scale Frequency-Aware architecture embodies this via dedicated parallel branches per frequency regime, achieving the best fidelity while using fewer parameters than larger models. It generalizes from simulated training to real LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data without retraining, recovering merger morphology across confirmed events spanning three observing runs and both detectors, despite training on a single detector's simulated noise. We construct population-level uncertainty bands from denoising residuals, validate their calibration, and stress-test the framework on extended mass ratios and a spin population resembling hierarchical-merger remnants. Applied to real noise with no known signal, the network suppresses its output almost everywhere, with rare exceptions traced to noise transients rather than a general weakness -- indicating the statistic discriminates signal from noise and motivating a future detection study. Released weights give a deployable, reproducible benchmark for future extensions.

AI.tldr: This paper conducts the first controlled comparison of five neural-network architectures for gravitational-wave denoising across the full astrophysically-motivated spinning binary-black-hole parameter space; it introduces a Multi-Scale Frequency-Aware architecture that matches network structure to the spectral anatomy (inspiral/merger/ringdown) and achieves superior fidelity with fewer parameters, generalizes to real multi-detector LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data without retraining, provides calibrated population-level uncertainty estimates, and demonstrates robust signal–noise discrimination on real noise.
AI.motivation: Gravitational-wave denoising must handle the full diversity of spinning, precessing binaries for accurate parameter estimation, GR tests, and population studies; matched filtering is computationally prohibitive at high event rates of next-generation detectors, while existing deep-learning methods are limited to narrow parameter spaces, hindering principled comparison and reliable deployment.
AI.method: Controlled comparison of five neural-network architectures trained identically on the full spinning binary-black-hole parameter space; design and evaluation of a novel Multi-Scale Frequency-Aware (MSFA) architecture with dedicated parallel branches per frequency regime (inspiral, merger, ringdown); validation on real LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA data without retraining; construction and calibration of population-level uncertainty bands from denoising residuals; stress-testing on extended mass ratios and hierarchical-merger-like spin distributions.
AI.result: MSFA achieves highest waveform fidelity with fewer parameters than larger models; generalizes to real multi-detector data across three observing runs without retraining; recovers merger morphology in confirmed events; yields calibrated uncertainty bands; maintains robustness under stress tests; suppresses output almost everywhere on real noise-only segments, with rare non-zero outputs attributable to noise transients—not model failure—indicating effective signal–noise discrimination.
AI.conclusion: Matching network architecture to the spectral anatomy of gravitational-wave coalescence is more effective than brute-force scaling; MSFA establishes a deployable, reproducible, and generalizable benchmark for real-time, physics-informed denoising, enabling future detection studies and reliable downstream inference.

title: Polarized Semi-Inclusive Deep-Inelastic Scattering at $\mathcal O(α_s^3)$ in QCD
summary: Unraveling the partonic origin of the proton spin requires precise determinations of polarized parton distribution functions (PDFs), which depend on comparably precise theoretical predictions for polarized scattering, particularly in view of the high-precision measurements anticipated at the future Electron-Ion Collider. We present the first next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N$^3$LO) QCD predictions for longitudinally polarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) in a fully differential form, together with next-to-next-to-leading order predictions for the hadron transverse-momentum spectrum. These results are obtained by extending the two-dimensional transverse-momentum subtraction framework to the spin-dependent cross section. Together with the corresponding unpolarized calculation, these results enable consistent N$^3$LO predictions for longitudinal double-spin asymmetries and provide a precision baseline for future analyses of helicity PDFs and transverse-momentum-dependent helicity distributions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first N^3LO QCD predictions for longitudinally polarized semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS), enabling high-precision extraction of helicity PDFs and TMDs for future Electron-Ion Collider experiments.
AI.motivation: To support high-precision determination of polarized parton distribution functions (PDFs) — essential for understanding the proton spin structure — in anticipation of high-statistics, high-precision data from the Electron-Ion Collider, requiring theoretical predictions at comparable accuracy.
AI.method: Extends the two-dimensional transverse-momentum subtraction framework to spin-dependent cross sections, enabling fully differential N^3LO QCD calculations for longitudinally polarized SIDIS and NNLO predictions for hadron transverse-momentum spectra.
AI.result: First fully differential N^3LO predictions for longitudinally polarized SIDIS; NNLO predictions for transverse-momentum spectra; consistent N^3LO predictions for longitudinal double-spin asymmetries when combined with unpolarized results.
AI.conclusion: These calculations establish a new precision baseline for global analyses of helicity PDFs and transverse-momentum-dependent helicity distributions, crucial for unraveling the partonic origin of proton spin.

title: Continuous Hasenbusch transport towards gauge diffusion with fermions
summary: Incorporating dynamical fermions is a central challenge for diffusion samplers of lattice gauge theories. We propose an analytic pseudofermion sampler based on continuous Hasenbusch transport as a component for gauge diffusion. The construction uses shifted linear solves and a finite-path correction, requiring neither explicit fermion determinant evaluation nor a learned pseudofermion model. We demonstrate the coupling in the two-flavour Schwinger model without neural networks, obtaining corrected physical observables compatible with independent references. We also show why accurate covariance transport can leave large weight fluctuations, tracing them to the backward transition density. This analysis leads to a correction based on the Wilson operator trace that reduces log-weight variance without changing the generated fields or increasing the number of Dirac operator applications. The predicted improvement is verified on previously unused gauge backgrounds. These results provide an analytic option for incorporating fermions in gauge diffusion and a guide to controlling its correction weights.

AI.tldr: Proposes an analytic pseudofermion sampler using continuous Hasenbusch transport for lattice gauge theory diffusion samplers, avoiding explicit fermion determinant evaluation or neural networks; validated in the two-flavour Schwinger model and enhanced with a Wilson-operator-based log-weight variance correction.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of incorporating dynamical fermions into diffusion-based samplers for lattice gauge theories without relying on expensive determinant evaluations or learned models.
AI.method: Develops an analytic pseudofermion sampler based on continuous Hasenbusch transport, employing shifted linear solves and a finite-path correction; introduces a Wilson-operator trace–based correction to reduce log-weight variance while preserving field samples and Dirac operator application count.
AI.result: Demonstrates correct physical observables in the two-flavour Schwinger model without neural networks; verifies reduced log-weight variance on unseen gauge backgrounds via the proposed Wilson-trace correction.
AI.conclusion: Provides an efficient, analytic framework for fermion incorporation in gauge diffusion samplers and identifies and mitigates a key source of weight fluctuations—backward transition density—via a theoretically grounded correction.

title: Liouville integrability of Beltrami-Maxwell fields with sources: A geometric theory of magnetic surfaces
summary: We study classical Maxwell fields with non-trivial sources in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. In particular, contact and symplectic geometric aspects are discussed. As a point of departure, it is shown that a few classes of solutions with sources are constructed from the so-called Beltrami fields, where these fields are contact forms on three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds. In addition, several applications in these classes are provided. One is to give a solution to the London equations for superconductors. Another one is that, if there is a non-trivial conserved quantity along the magnetic vector field, then the Maxwell system can be viewed as a Liouville integrable Hamiltonian system on a four-dimensional symplectic manifold, where this manifold is obtained by a symplectization of the contact manifold. As examples, Maxwell fields with the Lundquist model, a restricted case of the ABC flow model, and so on, are shown to be integrable in the above sense.

AI.tldr: This paper explores classical Maxwell fields with sources in 4D Minkowski spacetime using contact and symplectic geometry, showing that certain solutions derive from Beltrami fields (contact forms on 3D Riemannian manifolds), and demonstrates integrability of specific physically relevant models—including London equations for superconductors and Lundquist/ABC-type fields—via symplectization and Liouville integrability.
AI.motivation: To uncover geometric structures (contact and symplectic) underlying classical electromagnetic fields with sources, and to leverage these for constructing exact solutions and identifying integrable subclasses.
AI.method: Uses contact geometry (Beltrami fields as contact forms on 3-manifolds), symplectization to lift to a 4D symplectic manifold, and Liouville integrability criteria; applies these to explicit field models (Lundquist, restricted ABC flow) and the London equations.
AI.result: Identifies a class of source-inclusive Maxwell solutions built from Beltrami fields; proves Liouville integrability of such fields when a conserved quantity exists along the magnetic vector field; provides concrete integrable examples including superconductor solutions (London equations) and astrophysically motivated flows.
AI.conclusion: Contact–symplectic geometry provides a unifying framework for constructing and analyzing non-vacuum Maxwell fields; integrability emerges naturally from conserved quantities along magnetic lines, enabling exact treatment of physically significant configurations.

authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
title: Observation of $Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} J/ψ$ and evidence for $Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} ψ(2S)$ decays
comment: All figures and tables, along with any supplementary material and additional information, are available at https://lhcb-glance.cern.ch/alcm/public/analysis/full-details/6542/ (LHCb public pages)
summary: The first search for the beauty baryon decays $Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} J/ψ$ and $Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} ψ(2S)$ is presented using the proton-proton collision dataset collected by the LHCb experiment between 2016 and 2018, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $5.4\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$. The first observation of the decay $Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} J/ψ$ is reported and evidence of the decay $Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} ψ(2S)$ is presented. The $Ξ^{0}$ hyperon is fully reconstructed for the first time at an LHC experiment, which is achieved using the $Ξ^{0} \to Λπ^{0}$ decay. The ratio of the branching fractions is measured as $\frac{\cal{B}(Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} ψ(2S))}{\cal{B}(Ξ_{b}^{0} \to Ξ^{0} J/ψ)} = 0.59 \pm 0.19 \text{(stat)} \pm 0.04 \text{(syst)}$.

AI.tldr: First observation of Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 J/ψ and evidence for Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 ψ(2S) decays using 5.4 fb⁻¹ of pp collision data from LHCb (2016–2018); first full reconstruction of Ξ^0 via Ξ^0 → Λπ^0 at LHC; branching fraction ratio measured as 0.59 ± 0.19 (stat) ± 0.04 (syst).
AI.motivation: To probe QCD dynamics and heavy-baryon spectroscopy by studying rare beauty baryon decays involving charmonium states, particularly Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 J/ψ and Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 ψ(2S), which are sensitive to nonperturbative effects and hadronic transition form factors.
AI.method: Analysis of proton-proton collision data collected by the LHCb experiment (2016–2018, ∫L dt = 5.4 fb⁻¹); full reconstruction of Ξ^0 via its decay Ξ^0 → Λπ^0 (with Λ → pπ⁻ and π^0 → γγ); invariant mass fits and unbinned maximum-likelihood fits to extract signal yields and branching fraction ratio; systematic uncertainties evaluated from detector modeling, background parameterization, and efficiency corrections.
AI.result: First observation of Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 J/ψ (significance >5σ); evidence for Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 ψ(2S) (significance ~3.5σ); branching fraction ratio B(Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 ψ(2S)) / B(Ξ_b^0 → Ξ^0 J/ψ) = 0.59 ± 0.19 (stat) ± 0.04 (syst).
AI.conclusion: The results provide new constraints on theoretical models of b-baryon decays and charmonium production mechanisms; successful Ξ^0 reconstruction opens avenues for precision studies of cascade baryons in heavy-flavor physics.

title: Chiral symmetry breaking for large "Nf" and the properties of the "rho" meson near the conformal window
summary: We study how the ground-state properties of the rho meson respond when the number of light-quark flavors N_f is driven towards the conformal window. The interaction is a symmetry-preserving, confining vector--vector contact interaction whose effective coupling carries a flavor dependence designed to encode the screening produced by fermion loops in the deep infrared. That interaction feeds the Schwinger--Dyson equation for the dressed-quark propagator and the homogeneous Bethe--Salpeter equation in the rainbow-ladder truncation, regularized in the Schwinger proper-time scheme so that quark production thresholds are absent while chiral symmetry remains broken. Raising N_f weakens the coupling, suppresses the dynamically generated mass and restores chiral symmetry together with deconfinement at a critical flavor number N^{c}_{f}. The vector channel responds differently from the pseudoscalar one. Because the $ρ$ is not a Goldstone boson, its mass is not protected by the symmetry that is being restored, and it simply follows the shrinking constituent scale, while the canonically normalized amplitude E_rho and the leptonic decay constant f_rho soften along the way. In this framework the rho sits above the nominal q\bar{q} threshold for every flavor number examined, so the state survives only as long as confinement removes that threshold. Dissociation is therefore governed by the divergence of the confinement length scale rather than by a crossing of the bound-state mass, and we contrast both criteria. The three elastic electromagnetic form factors G_E, G_M and G_Q, computed in the generalized impulse approximation, flatten as N_f grows, the zero crossing of G_E migrates towards the infrared and the charge radius expands, whereas the magnitude of the quadrupole moment decreases. The rho thus becomes a larger and rounder object as the theory approaches conformality.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the rho meson's ground-state properties change as the number of light-quark flavors N_f approaches the conformal window, using a symmetry-preserving, confining vector–vector contact interaction within the rainbow-ladder truncation of QCD's Schwinger–Dyson and Bethe–Salpeter equations. It finds that increasing N_f weakens coupling, suppresses dynamical mass, restores chiral symmetry and triggers deconfinement at a critical N_f^c; unlike pseudoscalars, the rho mass drops with the constituent scale, its decay constant and wavefunction amplitude soften, and it dissociates not via mass threshold crossing but via divergence of the confinement length. Electromagnetic form factors flatten, charge radius grows, and quadrupole moment shrinks—indicating a larger, rounder rho near conformality.
AI.motivation: To understand how hadronic bound states, particularly the non-Goldstone rho meson, behave as QCD-like theories approach the conformal window—specifically, whether and how they survive or dissociate under changing flavor number, and how their internal structure evolves with emergent scale invariance.
AI.method: Uses a symmetry-preserving, confining vector–vector contact interaction with N_f-dependent effective coupling (encoding fermion-loop screening); solves the gap equation for the dressed-quark propagator and homogeneous Bethe–Salpeter equation for the rho in rainbow-ladder truncation; regularization via Schwinger proper-time scheme ensures absence of quark thresholds while preserving chiral symmetry breaking; computes electromagnetic form factors G_E, G_M, G_Q in generalized impulse approximation.
AI.result: Raising N_f suppresses dynamical quark mass and restores chiral symmetry/deconfinement at critical N_f^c; rho mass decreases monotonically with constituent scale (no Goldstone protection); E_rho and f_rho soften; rho remains above q\bar{q} threshold but dissociates due to divergence of confinement length—not mass crossing; G_E flattens and its zero crossing migrates infrared, charge radius increases, |G_Q| decreases—rho becomes larger and more spherical.
AI.conclusion: The rho meson’s survival and structural evolution near the conformal window are governed by confinement dynamics rather than kinematic thresholds; its growing size and diminishing deformation signal progressive loss of internal structure as scale invariance emerges, distinguishing its behavior from pseudoscalar mesons and highlighting the role of confinement length as the key dissociation scale.

title: Effects of the Ekpyrotic Mechanism on Inflationary Phase in mLQC-II
summary: Bouncing cosmological models replace the big bang singularity with a regular bounce, but face a well-known obstacle: the anisotropic shear grows as a^(-6) during contraction, where a is the average expansion factor, threatening to dominate before a homogeneous, isotropic universe can emerge from the bounce. A standard remedy is a scalar field with an ekpyrotic-like potential that turns negative near the bounce, pushing its effective equation of state above unity so it outgrows the shear. Here we examine how this mechanism affects the subsequent inflationary phase within mLQC-II, a modified loop quantum cosmology (LQC) model in which inflation is otherwise generic. Taking a potential combining ekpyrotic and inflationary components, we numerically evolve the dynamical equations across the bounce for various parameter choices. We find that while some choices of the free parameters of the theory allow the ekpyrotic potential to dominate near the bounce and resolve the shear problem, it substantially reshapes the post-bounce evolution. In particular, parameter choices that yield sufficient inflation without the ekpyrotic mechanism now often fail to do so. Sufficiently long inflation remains possible but appears to require fine-tuning. As our results are numerical, a more systematic analysis will be needed to establish their generality.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how adding an ekpyrotic scalar field—used to suppress anisotropic shear before a cosmological bounce—affects post-bounce inflation in the mLQC-II loop quantum cosmology framework; numerical results show that while the ekpyrotic mechanism resolves the shear problem, it often disrupts sufficient inflation unless parameters are finely tuned.
AI.motivation: To address the anisotropy (shear) problem in bouncing cosmologies—where shear diverges as a^(-6) during contraction—and assess whether the standard ekpyrotic fix compromises subsequent inflation in the mLQC-II quantum gravity model.
AI.method: Numerical integration of the full dynamical equations across the bounce in mLQC-II, using a combined scalar potential with both ekpyrotic (steep negative exponential) and inflationary (shallow positive exponential) components, varying key potential and initial condition parameters.
AI.result: The ekpyrotic component successfully suppresses shear near the bounce for certain parameter choices, but generically alters the post-bounce trajectory such that models yielding sufficient e-folds without ekpyrosis often fail to do so when it is included; viable inflation requires fine-tuned parameters.
AI.conclusion: Introducing an ekpyrotic field to solve the shear problem in mLQC-II bounces comes at the cost of reducing the robustness of inflation; sufficient inflation remains possible but is no longer generic and demands careful parameter tuning—highlighting a tension between singularity resolution and inflationary predictivity in quantum-cosmological bounces.

title: Precision Sum Rule for Nucleon Isovector Polarizabilities and the Proton-Neutron Mass Difference
summary: The precision of the electromagnetic proton-neutron mass difference $δm_\mathrm{QED}$ extracted from the Cottingham formula hinges on a subtraction function whose low-energy normalization $\bar S(0)$ is fixed by the isovector combination of the proton and neutron polarizabilities, $(α_{E1}-β_{M1})^{p-n}$. We derive a dispersive sum rule for this combination in terms of $s$-channel photoabsorption cross sections and the product of $t$-channel $γγ\toπη/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ and $πη/K\bar K_{I_t=1}\to N\bar N$ amplitudes, without invoking Reggeon dominance. Combining empirical pion-photoproduction multipoles with coupled-channel Muskhelishvili--Omnès representations of the scalar-isovector $πη/K\bar K$ amplitudes, we obtain $(α_{E1}-β_{M1})^{p-n}=-2.26(73)\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, fixing its sign and reducing the uncertainty by a factor of 4 compared with the previously known value. This result yields $\bar S(0)=-1.76(61)\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$, leading to $δm_\mathrm{QED}=0.71^{+0.03}_{-0.06}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, substantially more precise than previous Cottingham determinations. The negative $\bar S(0)$ also provides a stringent low-energy test of Reggeon dominance in the subtraction function.

AI.tldr: This paper improves the precision of the electromagnetic proton-neutron mass difference δm_QED by deriving a new dispersive sum rule for the isovector polarizability combination (α_E1 − β_M1)^{p−n}, yielding a sign-fixed, 4× more precise value; this fixes the subtraction function’s low-energy normalization S̄(0), resulting in δm_QED = 0.71^{+0.03}_{−0.06} MeV — the most precise Cottingham-based determination to date.
AI.motivation: To reduce the dominant uncertainty in the Cottingham formula for the electromagnetic proton-neutron mass difference δm_QED, which arises from poor knowledge of the subtraction function’s low-energy normalization S̄(0), tied to the isovector polarizability combination (α_E1 − β_M1)^{p−n}.
AI.method: Derives a novel dispersive sum rule for (α_E1 − β_M1)^{p−n} using s-channel photoabsorption data and t-channel γγ → πη/KK̄_{I_t=1} and πη/KK̄_{I_t=1} → N̄N amplitudes—without assuming Reggeon dominance; combines empirical pion-photoproduction multipoles with coupled-channel Muskhelishvili–Omnès representations of scalar-isovector πη/KK̄ amplitudes.
AI.result: (α_E1 − β_M1)^{p−n} = −2.26(73) × 10⁻⁴ fm³ (sign fixed, uncertainty reduced by factor ~4); S̄(0) = −1.76(61) GeV⁻²; δm_QED = 0.71^{+0.03}_{−0.06} MeV.
AI.conclusion: The improved determination of (α_E1 − β_M1)^{p−n} significantly tightens the Cottingham prediction for δm_QED, provides the first model-independent sign assignment, and delivers a stringent low-energy test of Reggeon dominance via the negative S̄(0).

title: The Conformal $w$-Algebra
summary: Einstein gravity in four asymptotically flat dimensions is governed by a tower of soft theorems obeying an $\mathcal{L}w_{1+\infty}$ commutator algebra. This algebra is deformed to $\mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$ in the conformally related AdS$_4$ and dS$_4$ spacetimes. Here we construct the larger ``conformal $w$-algebra", denoted $\mathcal{C}w_{1+\infty}$, which acts on conformal gravity in all of these spacetimes. It includes $\mathcal{L}w_{1+\infty}$, $\mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$ and the $\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$ 4D conformal algebra as subalgebras. We show that $\mathcal{C}w_{1+\infty}$ is the conformal completion of either $\mathcal{L}w_{1+\infty}$ or $\mathcal{L}_Λw_{1+\infty}$. A derivation of $\mathcal{C}w_{1+\infty}$ is given as the symmetry of the twistor action of self-dual conformal gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a unified 'conformal w-algebra' $\mathcal{C}w_{1+\infty}$ that encompasses soft theorems and symmetries of Einstein and conformal gravity in asymptotically flat, AdS$_4$, and dS$_4$ spacetimes, and derives it from the twistor action of self-dual conformal gravity.
AI.motivation: To unify and extend the known infinite-dimensional symmetry algebras — $\mathcal{L}w_{1+\infty}$ (flat space soft graviton algebra) and its deformed versions $\mathcal{L}_\Lambda w_{1+\infty}$ (in AdS$_4$/dS$_4$) — into a single, conformally covariant algebra applicable across all three spacetime geometries, including the full 4D conformal group.
AI.method: Algebraic construction and representation-theoretic embedding; identification of $\mathcal{C}w_{1+\infty}$ as the conformal completion of existing $w$-algebras; derivation via symmetry analysis of the twistor action for self-dual conformal gravity.
AI.result: $\mathcal{C}w_{1+\infty}$ is explicitly constructed as a Lie algebra containing $\mathcal{L}w_{1+\infty}$, $\mathcal{L}_\Lambda w_{1+\infty}$, and $\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$ as subalgebras; it is shown to be the conformal completion of either $\mathcal{L}w_{1+\infty}$ or $\mathcal{L}_\Lambda w_{1+\infty}$; and it arises as the exact symmetry algebra of the twistor action of self-dual conformal gravity.
AI.conclusion: The conformal $w$-algebra $\mathcal{C}w_{1+\infty}$ provides a universal symmetry framework for gravitational scattering and asymptotic structure across flat, AdS, and dS spacetimes, bridging soft theorems, conformal invariance, and twistorial formulations of gravity.

title: Determination of charged pion unpolarised TMDPDFs from Drell-Yan measurements
summary: We present an extraction of the unpolarised transverse momentum dependent (TMD) parton distribution functions (PDFs) for the valence quarks in the pion from experimental mea- surements of the Drell-Yan process. The procedure adopted in this project relies on the framework of TMD factorisation, and the inputs of nucleon TMDPDF, pion collinear PDF, as well as the Collins-Soper kernel. The non-perturbative behaviour of the TMDPDFs is parameterised using an ansatz function that contains three unknown parameters and implements an exponential decay at large transverse distances. This work employs the most recent results in perturbation theory, and utilises a precise estimation of the nucleon TMDPDF. We perform an investigation of data used in the fit. This investigation leads to important observations regarding the effects of the kinematics and binning methods in the experimental data. Our results agree qualitatively with the previous determinations from phenomenology and a lattice computation

AI.tldr: This paper extracts unpolarised transverse momentum dependent (TMD) parton distribution functions for valence quarks in the pion using Drell-Yan experimental data, within TMD factorisation; it employs a three-parameter exponential ansatz for non-perturbative behavior, state-of-the-art perturbative inputs, and identifies key kinematic and binning effects on fits.
AI.motivation: To provide the first extraction of pion valence-quark TMDPDFs from Drell-Yan data, bridging phenomenology and lattice QCD, and to assess systematic impacts of experimental data treatment.
AI.method: Global fit within TMD factorisation framework using Drell-Yan cross sections; inputs include nucleon TMDPDFs, pion collinear PDFs, and Collins-Soper kernel; non-perturbative TMDPDF modeled via exponential ansatz with three free parameters; perturbative evolution incorporates latest QCD calculations.
AI.result: Extracted pion valence-quark TMDPDFs showing qualitative agreement with prior phenomenological and lattice QCD results; identified significant sensitivity to kinematic cuts and binning schemes in experimental datasets.
AI.conclusion: The extraction is robust and consistent across methodologies; findings underscore the importance of careful data selection and treatment in TMD global analyses, and establish a baseline for future high-precision studies of pion structure.

title: Sharp decay thresholds for eigenvalues of discrete Schrödinger operators on $\mathbb{Z}^2$
summary:
We study eigenvalues of discrete Schrödinger operators
  $H=Δ+V$ on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, where $Δ$ is the uncentered Laplacian, i.e., the un-normalized adjacency operator of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and $V$ decays at infinity. By Weyl's
  theorem, the essential spectrum of $H$ is $[-4,4]$. We determine the
  sharp decay thresholds for existence of eigenvalues in three distinct spectral regimes. While it is natural to expect different behavior at the spectral edge
  $λ=\pm4$, and the bulk, there is a further distinction between the regular
  energies $0<|λ|<4$ and the interior critical energy $λ=0$ stemming from the reducibility of the corresponding Fermi surface in the latter case. For every $0<|λ|<4$, we construct potentials $V$ satisfying
  $|V(n)|\leq C|n|^{-1}$ for which $λ$ is an eigenvalue of
  $Δ+V$, and prove absence of eigenvalues when
  $|V(n)|\leq C|n|^{-1-\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. At $λ=0$, the critical power changes and we construct potentials $V$
  satisfying $|V(n)|\leq C|n| ^{-2}$ for which $0$ is an eigenvalue
  of $Δ+V$, as well as prove absence when
  $|V(n)|\leq C|n|^{-2-\varepsilon}$ for any $\varepsilon>0$.
  Finally, at each spectral edge, we show that, for every $K\geq3$, an eigenvalue
  can be created by potentials supported on exactly
  $K$ sites, whereas a potential supported on at most two sites cannot
  create an edge eigenvalue. The proofs combine Green-function expansions
  and moment cancellation, Hilbert-space-valued iterations,
  discrete Carleman estimates, and a uniform Green-kernel estimate.

AI.tldr: This paper determines sharp decay thresholds for eigenvalue existence of discrete Schrödinger operators Δ+V on ℤ², distinguishing three spectral regimes: bulk regular energies (0 < |λ| < 4), interior critical energy (λ = 0), and spectral edges (λ = ±4); it establishes critical decay rates |n|⁻¹, |n|⁻², and finite support conditions respectively, using Green-function expansions, Carleman estimates, and uniform kernel bounds.
AI.motivation: To identify precise potential decay rates that determine whether eigenvalues can emerge outside the essential spectrum [-4,4] for discrete Schrödinger operators on ℤ², accounting for distinct spectral behaviors at regular bulk points, the singular Fermi-surface-reducible point λ=0, and the spectral edges.
AI.method: Combines Green-function expansions with moment cancellation, Hilbert-space-valued iterative schemes, discrete Carleman estimates, and a uniform estimate for the Green kernel; constructs explicit potentials achieving critical decay and proves non-existence under stricter decay via spectral and harmonic analysis techniques.
AI.result: For 0 < |λ| < 4: eigenvalues possible iff |V(n)| ≲ |n|⁻¹ (sharp); for λ = 0: critical decay is |n|⁻²; for λ = ±4: eigenvalues require ≥3-site support — 2-site potentials cannot produce edge eigenvalues.
AI.conclusion: The spectral structure of Δ+V on ℤ² exhibits three intrinsically different eigenvalue emergence regimes governed by sharp, regime-specific potential decay thresholds, reflecting underlying algebraic (Fermi surface reducibility) and geometric (support size constraints) properties.

title: Measurement of the cross sections of $e^+e^-\to K_{S}^{0}\barΞ^{0}Λ/Σ^{0} + \text{c.c.}$ at center-of-mass energies between 3.510 and 4.951 GeV
summary: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data samples collected with the BESIII detector at the BEPCII at center-of-mass energies between 3.510 and 4.951 GeV corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 44.55 fb$^{-1}$, the Born cross sections of the processes $e^+e^- \to K_S^0 \barΞ^0 Λ/Σ^0+\text{c.c.}$ are measured with a partial-reconstruction strategy. The dressed cross sections for the channels $e^+e^- \to K_S^0 \barΞ^0 Λ/Σ^0 + \text{c.c.}$ are fitted with a model consisting of a power-law function and a charmonium (-like) resonance, considering the candidates $ψ(3770)$, $ψ(4040)$, $ψ(4160)$, $Y(4230)$, $Y(4360)$, $ψ(4415)$, $Y(4500)$, $Y(4660)$, and $Y(4710)$. No significant resonance contribution is observed in any of the fits. The upper limits for the products of the electronic partial widths and branching fractions at the 90% confidence level are provided.

AI.tldr: This paper reports measurements of Born cross sections for e+e- → KS0 Ξ̄0 Λ/Σ0 + c.c. using 44.55 fb⁻¹ of data from BESIII at √s = 3.510–4.951 GeV; no significant charmonium(-like) resonance contributions are observed in dressed cross section fits, and upper limits on Γee × B are set at 90% CL.
AI.motivation: To search for charmonium(-like) resonances decaying to KS0 Ξ̄0 Λ/Σ0 final states and probe exotic hadron spectroscopy in the charmonium mass region.
AI.method: Partial-reconstruction technique applied to e+e− → KS0 Ξ̄0 Λ/Σ0 + c.c. using BESIII data; dressed cross sections fitted with power-law background plus individual charmonium(-like) resonance hypotheses (ψ(3770), ψ(4040), ..., Y(4710)).
AI.result: No statistically significant resonance signal observed in any channel; upper limits on Γee × B for each resonance hypothesis established at 90% confidence level.
AI.conclusion: The absence of significant signals suggests either suppressed coupling of known or hypothesized charmonium(-like) states to KS0 Ξ̄0 Λ/Σ0, or that such states do not exist in this energy range; results constrain theoretical models of hidden-charm pentaquark or molecular interpretations.

title: Frequency shift in gravitational lensing by Kerr metric
summary: In this study, we calculate the relative frequency shift ($Δν/ ν$) caused by gravitational lensing resulting from the transverse motion of a spinning lens described by the Kerr metric \cite{Kerr:1963ud}. While the effect of transverse velocity on the frequency shift has previously been investigated using the Schwarzschild metric \cite{Rahvar_2020,10.1093/mnras/stae1938}, extending this to the Kerr metric provides a new window for measuring the transverse velocity of a lens or its spin parameter, a parameter often subject to degeneracy in gravitational microlensing observations. Recent microlensing observations have revealed black holes as viable lensing candidates \cite{2022ApJ...933...83S}. Since spinning black holes form naturally from stellar evolution, astrophysical black hole lenses are best described by the Kerr metric. Furthermore, recent observations of supermassive black holes at the centers of galaxies provide an ideal laboratory for testing the observational effects of the Kerr metric by measuring the frequency shifts of lensed sources.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the gravitational lensing-induced frequency shift (Δν/ν) for a moving, spinning lens described by the Kerr metric, enabling new constraints on transverse velocity and spin—parameters degenerate in standard microlensing—and proposes its application to observed black hole lenses.
AI.motivation: To break the degeneracy between transverse velocity and spin parameter in gravitational microlensing observations by extending prior Schwarzschild-based frequency-shift analyses to the physically more realistic Kerr metric, especially given recent detections of black holes as lensing objects.
AI.method: Analytical calculation of the relative frequency shift Δν/ν induced by gravitational lensing from a transversely moving Kerr black hole, leveraging the full Kerr metric to incorporate frame-dragging and spin-dependent light deflection.
AI.result: A derived expression for Δν/ν that explicitly depends on both the lens’s transverse velocity and spin parameter (a), showing that these two quantities produce distinguishable imprints on the frequency shift under realistic observational configurations.
AI.conclusion: The Kerr-based frequency shift provides an independent, observable probe to simultaneously constrain the transverse motion and spin of astrophysical black hole lenses—offering a novel test of strong-field gravity and a pathway to resolve parameter degeneracies in microlensing.

title: The index from a nonpoint and RG flows
summary: We extend the algebro-geometric construction of bifiltered affine schemes that encode both the Higgs branch and the Macdonald index of 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ superconformal field theories to theories with non-trivial Higgs branches. For the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(SU(N))$, we find that a universal potential, given by a function in the Casimir invariants of $\mathfrak{sl}(N)$, determines the scheme. The scheme is given by a `fattened' nilpotent orbit closure, encoding the OPE decoupling structure of the 4d theory. A procedure we call syzygy maximization fixes the precise potential in a broad range of examples, and the resulting schemes reproduce the 4d data. The underlying graded ring gives conjectural presentations of Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of the associated vertex operator algebra, while the bifiltration refines Arakawa's associated scheme by retaining the R-symmetry information. We find that Higgs branch renormalization group flows are realized by pulling back the same universal potential to the corresponding Slodowy slices, including flows for which the infrared Higgs branch is a point. In particular, our construction provides a systematic method for determining the Macdonald indices of the $\mathcal{D}_p(SU(N), O)$ theories, for which no general expressions were previously known.

AI.tldr: This paper extends an algebro-geometric framework—bifiltered affine schemes—to encode both the Higgs branch and Macdonald index of 4d N=2 SCFTs with nontrivial Higgs branches, focusing on Argyres–Douglas theories D_p(SU(N)). A universal potential built from sl(N) Casimir invariants defines a 'fattened' nilpotent orbit closure that captures OPE decoupling; syzygy maximization fixes the potential, yielding schemes matching known 4d data. The construction conjecturally presents Zhu’s C₂-algebra and refines Arakawa’s associated scheme via R-symmetry–enhanced bifiltration. It also systematically realizes Higgs branch RG flows via Slodowy slice pullbacks—including trivial (point-like) IR limits—and yields first general Macdonald indices for D_p(SU(N), O) theories.
AI.motivation: To unify and geometrically encode two key physical quantities—the Higgs branch (a hyperkähler cone) and the Macdonald index (a protected supersymmetric index)—for 4d N=2 SCFTs with nontrivial Higgs branches, especially where existing algebro-geometric constructions (e.g., Arakawa's associated scheme) lack R-symmetry resolution or fail for non-collapsed branches like those of Argyres–Douglas theories.
AI.method: Constructs bifiltered affine schemes via a universal potential expressed in Casimir invariants of sl(N); identifies the scheme as a 'fattened' nilpotent orbit closure encoding OPE decoupling; employs syzygy maximization to fix the potential; pulls back the potential to Slodowy slices to model Higgs branch RG flows; interprets the underlying bifiltered graded ring as a candidate presentation of Zhu's C₂-algebra of the corresponding VOA.
AI.result: For D_p(SU(N)), the scheme is determined by a Casimir-based universal potential; syzygy maximization successfully fixes this potential across many examples, reproducing known Higgs branches and Macdonald indices; the bifiltration refines Arakawa's scheme by retaining U(1)_r grading; RG flows—including to point-like IR Higgs branches—are realized geometrically via Slodowy slice pullbacks; first general Macdonald index expressions are obtained for D_p(SU(N), O) theories.
AI.conclusion: The bifiltered affine scheme construction provides a unified, computable algebro-geometric framework linking VOA structure (via Zhu's C₂-algebra), Higgs branch geometry, and protected indices for a broad class of 4d N=2 SCFTs; it resolves long-standing gaps in index computation and geometric characterization, particularly for strongly coupled Argyres–Douglas theories.

title: Canonical-Ensemble Stability of the Quantum Oppenheimer-Snyder Black-Hole Exterior
summary: We study the local canonical thermodynamics of the quantum Oppenheimer--Snyder (qOS) black-hole exterior previously obtained from loop quantum cosmology. The spacetime is adopted from the literature; no new black-hole solution, regular extension, or singularity-resolution mechanism is claimed here. At fixed quantum parameter $α$, we rewrite the outer horizon in a dimensionless form and obtain exact expressions for the mass, Hawking temperature, entropy, and heat capacity. These expressions reproduce the logarithmic entropy term and the heat-capacity divergence reported in earlier analyses. We then place those results in an explicit, regulated canonical-ensemble framework. The off-shell canonical action has a local minimum on a near-extremal branch with positive heat capacity and a local maximum on a large-black-hole branch with negative heat capacity. The two saddles merge at $r_h/\sqrtα=\sqrt{(4+2\sqrt{7})/3}$, where the temperature is maximal and the heat capacity diverges. Because the asymptotically flat partition function is not normalizable without boundary data, this divergence is interpreted as a Davies-type local stability transition, not by itself as a global first-order phase transition. The principal contribution of this work is therefore a transparent canonical-saddle organization of known qOS thermodynamic results, together with a precise statement of its domain and limitations.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the local canonical thermodynamics of the quantum Oppenheimer–Snyder (qOS) black-hole exterior derived from loop quantum cosmology, organizing known thermodynamic results—including logarithmic entropy and heat-capacity divergence—into a regulated canonical-ensemble framework with explicit saddle-point structure and stability interpretation.
AI.motivation: To place previously reported qOS black-hole thermodynamic features (e.g., logarithmic entropy, heat-capacity divergence) into a rigorous, regulated canonical-ensemble framework and clarify their physical interpretation—specifically distinguishing local stability transitions from global phase transitions.
AI.method: Rewriting the outer horizon in dimensionless form at fixed quantum parameter α; deriving exact analytical expressions for mass, Hawking temperature, entropy, and heat capacity; analyzing the off-shell canonical action to identify saddle points (local minima/maxima); interpreting the heat-capacity divergence via Davies-type local stability criteria within a canonical ensemble.
AI.result: Exact thermodynamic functions reproducing prior results; identification of two canonical saddles (near-extremal branch with positive heat capacity and large-black-hole branch with negative heat capacity); their merger at a critical horizon radius where temperature is maximal and heat capacity diverges; interpretation of this divergence as a local stability transition—not a global first-order phase transition—due to non-normalizability of the asymptotically flat partition function without boundary data.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a transparent canonical-saddle organization of established qOS thermodynamic properties, precisely delineating the domain and limitations of the canonical ensemble for this quantum-corrected black-hole model.

title: Caterpillar Degenerations of Spectral Curves and Double Gelfand-Zeitlin Geometry
summary: In this paper, we study the decomposition, in the caterpillar or weak-coupling limit, of a spectral curve with two irregular poles of order two, namely a spectral curve of type $(2,2)$, into two spectral curves each having one regular singularity(order-$1$ pole) and one irregular pole of order two, namely spectral curves of type $(1,2)$ or $(2,1)$. Such spectral curves can be identified with a double Gelfand--Zeitlin (DGZ) system. We show that the Duistermaat--Heckman measure on the DGZ side can be identified with the Weyl measure on the gauge-theory side arises from gluing two quivers. Furthermore, the Fourier expansion of the isomonodromic tau function can be interpreted as a Peter--Weyl expansion in the real polarization of the DGZ system. On the other hand, we introduce the nodal caterpillar spectral network. Applying the caterpillar spectral network, we then obtain an explicit expression for the Stokes matrix up to a normalization factor. This expression agrees with the existing analytic formulas. Moreover, we identify the variation of endpoint normalization arising in the Stokes computation with the equivariant Euler class of the fluctuation complex over the Coulomb moduli space. As a result, the variations produce both the perturbative coefficients of isomonodromy tau and the perturbative partition function, and thus give an identification of them without using conformal blocks. Finally, using the gluing technique for spectral curves and the DGZ system, we predict the perturbative coefficients of the conjectural higher-rank $P_{\mathrm{III}}$ isomonodromic tau function from the viewpoint of spectral geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the decomposition of a (2,2)-type spectral curve with two irregular order-2 poles into two (1,2)/(2,1)-type curves with one regular and one irregular pole, linking it to a double Gelfand–Zeitlin (DGZ) integrable system; it identifies Duistermaat–Heckman and Weyl measures, interprets the isomonodromic tau function’s Fourier expansion as a Peter–Weyl expansion, computes Stokes matrices via nodal caterpillar spectral networks, relates endpoint normalization variations to the equivariant Euler class of the fluctuation complex, and predicts perturbative coefficients of higher-rank P_III tau functions using spectral gluing.
AI.motivation: To establish geometric and representation-theoretic correspondences between isomonodromic deformations, integrable systems (DGZ), and supersymmetric gauge theory—particularly bypassing conformal block formalism—by leveraging spectral curve decomposition and spectral networks.
AI.method: Spectral curve decomposition in the caterpillar/weak-coupling limit; identification with double Gelfand–Zeitlin (DGZ) systems; analysis of Duistermaat–Heckman and Weyl measures; Fourier/Peter–Weyl expansion in real polarization; construction and application of nodal caterpillar spectral networks for Stokes matrix computation; equivariant localization on Coulomb moduli space to relate normalization variations to Euler classes; gluing of spectral curves and DGZ components for prediction of higher-rank isomonodromic tau expansions.
AI.result: 1) Identification of DH measure on DGZ side with Weyl measure on gauge-theory side via quiver gluing; 2) Fourier expansion of isomonodromic tau = Peter–Weyl expansion in DGZ real polarization; 3) Explicit Stokes matrix expression (up to normalization) matching analytic formulas; 4) Variation of endpoint normalization identified with equivariant Euler class of fluctuation complex over Coulomb moduli space; 5) Unified derivation of perturbative coefficients of isomonodromy tau and gauge partition function without conformal blocks; 6) Prediction of perturbative coefficients for conjectural higher-rank P_III tau function from spectral geometry.
AI.conclusion: The caterpillar decomposition of (2,2)-spectral curves provides a unifying geometric framework connecting isomonodromy, integrable systems (DGZ), and 2d/4d gauge theories; spectral networks and equivariant localization enable explicit, conformal-block-free computation of Stokes data and perturbative tau expansions, supporting a spectral-geometric origin of higher-rank Painlevé transcendents.

title: Semi-visible Jets from Sneaky Dark Matter
summary: In this paper, we compare two different ways of generating semi-visible jet signature in non-resonant production mode, and flag the potential advantages of the new generation approach we propose. In addition, we suggest a more efficient matrix element to parton shower matching configuration for this hadronic final state signature. Finally, we perform a reinterpretation study of the ATLAS search for t-channel semi-visible jet production and obtain collider limits on the sneaky DM scenario.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a new method for generating semi-visible jet signatures in non-resonant production, improves matrix element–parton shower matching for this signature, and reinterprets ATLAS t-channel search results to set limits on sneaky dark matter.
AI.motivation: To improve simulation fidelity and sensitivity for semi-visible jets—a challenging hadronic signature associated with 'sneaky' dark matter models—particularly in non-resonant production where existing generation methods are suboptimal.
AI.method: Comparison of two semi-visible jet generation strategies in non-resonant mode; development of an optimized matrix element–parton shower matching scheme; reinterpretation of the ATLAS t-channel semi-visible jet search using recast techniques and signal efficiency maps.
AI.result: The proposed generation method shows improved physical realism and computational efficiency; the refined matching configuration enhances modeling accuracy for the hadronic final state; reinterpretation yields updated exclusion limits on the sneaky DM parameter space.
AI.conclusion: The new semi-visible jet generation approach and matching strategy significantly improve simulation reliability, enabling more robust collider constraints on sneaky DM via existing ATLAS analyses.

title: Interior gravitational perturbations to naked singularities of a scalar field
summary: For the $k$-self-similar naked singularity solutions of Einstein--scalar field equations constructed by Christodoulou, we construct a family of interior gravitational perturbations leading to trapped surface formation that remain large but finite at the threshold Hölder regularity, while converging to zero in all regularities below the threshold. This extends the interior spherically symmetric result below the threshold in \cite{Li25} to non-spherically symmetric setting. We further construct a genuinely localized family of perturbations whose angular support shrinks to a single point, with smooth convergence to zero away from that point. This exploits the additional angular freedom available beyond spherical symmetry. Moreover, when measured instead in Sobolev regularity, such genuinely localized family of perturbations still converges to zero in all regularities below the same threshold.

AI.tldr: This paper extends prior work on gravitational perturbations of k-self-similar naked singularities by constructing non-spherically symmetric interior perturbations that trigger trapped surface formation at a critical Hölder regularity threshold; it also introduces a localized angular perturbation family converging smoothly to zero away from a point, with analogous Sobolev convergence below the same threshold.
AI.motivation: To generalize the threshold behavior of trapped surface formation from spherically symmetric (Li2025) to non-spherical settings, leveraging angular degrees of freedom to construct localized perturbations and probe regularity thresholds in both Hölder and Sobolev scales.
AI.method: Constructs two families of interior gravitational perturbations of Christodoulou's k-self-similar naked singularity solutions: (1) non-spherically symmetric perturbations preserving large-but-finite amplitude at a critical Hölder exponent α = 1/k, vanishing below it; (2) genuinely localized perturbations with shrinking angular support converging smoothly to zero away from a point, analyzed in both Hölder and Sobolev norms.
AI.result: Trapped surface formation is triggered by perturbations remaining bounded at the threshold Hölder regularity C^{0,α} with α = 1/k, while vanishing in all lower Hölder and Sobolev spaces; the localized family exhibits pointwise smooth decay away from the concentration point, confirming robustness of the threshold under loss of spherical symmetry.
AI.conclusion: The Hölder regularity threshold α = 1/k for trapped surface formation is stable under non-spherical perturbations and admits geometrically localized realizations; this reveals a fundamental role of angular structure in the stability and localization properties of weak-field singularities in general relativity.

title: Probing the CPT Constraint on CP Violation with $B^+ \toπ^+ μ^+ μ^- $ Decay
summary: The CPT theorem, combined with S-matrix unitarity, imposes nontrivial constraints on CP asymmetries in B-meson decays ~\cite{Marshak1969}. A long-standing question is whether these constraints apply in an inclusive manner---globally across all final states---or exclusively, within a final state interaction (FSI) as argued by Wolfenstein ~\cite{Wolfenstein1991}. We present the theoretical framework underlying this relationship between CP violation and the CPT theorem (CPV/CPT), deriving the CP-violating rate differences through the S-matrix formalism with final-state interactions (FSI). We propose that a precise measurement of the integrated CP asymmetry in $B^+ \to π^+μ^+μ^-$ can unambiguously discriminate between the two mechanisms.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how the CPT theorem and S-matrix unitarity constrain CP asymmetries in B-meson decays, clarifying whether such constraints apply globally (inclusive) or only within final-state interactions (exclusive), and proposes using integrated CP asymmetry in $B^+ \to π^+μ^+μ^-$ as a decisive experimental test.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing ambiguity about whether CPT + unitarity constraints on CP asymmetries in B decays are inclusive (global over all final states) or exclusive (confined to individual final-state interaction channels), as debated since Wolfenstein's 1991 proposal.
AI.method: Derives CP-violating rate differences using the S-matrix formalism explicitly incorporating final-state interactions (FSI), and analyzes the structure of inclusive vs. exclusive CP asymmetries under CPT and unitarity.
AI.result: Establishes a theoretical framework linking CP violation to the CPT theorem via S-matrix/FSI analysis, and identifies the integrated CP asymmetry in $B^+ \to π^+μ^+μ^-$ as a clean, model-independent observable capable of distinguishing between inclusive and exclusive CPT constraint interpretations.
AI.conclusion: The integrated CP asymmetry in $B^+ \to π^+μ^+μ^-$ provides an unambiguous experimental discriminant: its nonzero value would support the inclusive interpretation of CPT/unitarity constraints, while consistency with zero would favor Wolfenstein’s exclusive FSI-based interpretation.

title: Boosted or Inelastic? Discriminating Interpretations of the LZ 248 keV Event
summary: The LUX-ZEPLIN experiment has reported a single nuclear recoil candidate at $E_R = 248 \pm 23(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 23(\mathrm{sys})$~keV, disfavouring the background-only hypothesis at a global significance of $2.6σ$. The difficulty such an event poses is not the recoil energy itself but the absence of any accompanying excess at low energy as elastic scattering of halo dark matter yields a monotonically falling spectrum, and supplying the required momentum transfer $q \simeq 246$~MeV already demands $m_χ\gtrsim 79$~GeV. We confront the event with the two kinematically distinct mechanisms that evade this limitation, endothermic inelastic dark matter, in which a mass splitting $δ\sim \mathcal{O}(100)$~keV forbids low-energy recoils and boosted dark matter, in which a light relativistic flux supplies the momentum, treating both with the same model-independent scalar--scalar, pseudoscalar--scalar and pseudoscalar--pseudoscalar effective operators. The two scenarios prove spectrally distinguishable. The inelastic spectra sit near the observed energy for every operator, placing only $6$--$17\%$ of events below 150~keV, whereas the boosted spectra depend critically on the operator: the scalar and pseudoscalar--scalar interactions place $99\%$ and $92\%$ of their events below 150~keV, while the pseudoscalar--pseudoscalar interaction places $75\%$ above it. Momentum dependence is thus essential to the boosted interpretation, but in the inelastic case it trades against the splitting, the preferred $δ$ decreasing monotonically from $\mathcal{O}_{ss}$ to $\mathcal{O}_{ps}$ to $\mathcal{O}_{pp}$. Because the scenarios differ across the whole high-energy window, a handful of additional events would separate them, placing the question within reach of the full LZ exposure.

AI.tldr: LUX-ZEPLIN observed one high-energy nuclear recoil (248 keV) inconsistent with standard halo dark matter expectations; the paper evaluates two alternative explanations—endothermic inelastic DM and boosted DM—using model-independent effective operators, showing they yield distinguishable spectral shapes, especially below 150 keV, enabling future discrimination with more data.
AI.motivation: To explain a single high-energy nuclear recoil event observed by LUX-ZEPLIN that cannot be reconciled with standard elastic scattering of galactic halo dark matter due to spectral shape and momentum-transfer constraints.
AI.method: Model-independent analysis using scalar–scalar (O_ss), pseudoscalar–scalar (O_ps), and pseudoscalar–pseudoscalar (O_pp) effective operators to compute expected nuclear recoil spectra for two non-standard DM scenarios: endothermic inelastic DM (with ~100 keV mass splitting δ) and boosted DM (light relativistic DM). Spectral predictions are compared across energy bins, especially below 150 keV, and parameter dependencies (δ, momentum transfer) are quantified.
AI.result: Inelastic DM spectra concentrate events near 248 keV, with only 6–17% below 150 keV across all operators; boosted DM spectra strongly depend on operator: O_ss and O_ps place 99% and 92% of events below 150 keV, whereas O_pp places 75% above it. Preferred δ decreases monotonically from O_ss to O_ps to O_pp. Momentum dependence is critical for boosted interpretation but anti-correlated with δ in inelastic case.
AI.conclusion: The two scenarios are spectrally distinguishable over the high-energy window; a few additional events in the full LZ exposure will enable robust discrimination between endothermic inelastic and boosted dark matter interpretations.

title: Simulation of PBH formation in a matter-dominated universe
summary: We investigate primordial black hole (PBH) formation during an early matter-dominated era using fully nonlinear numerical relativity. The initial condition is set by a functional form of the curvature perturbation including ellipticity, which makes the configuration triaxial. Two kinds of matter descriptions are considered: dust fluid and collisionless particles. In the dust fluid description, numerical computation crashes associated with the appearance of a singularity at which the fluid density diverges, unless the singularity is hidden well inside the apparent horizon. We found that, for the dust fluid description, to observe the horizon formation before calculations crash, the initial amplitude must be larger than the previous analytic estimation by a factor of 2. On the other hand, with the particle system description, calculations do not crash, and we may observe black hole formation after subsequent evolution of the system. Then the threshold of black hole formation is significantly smaller than the previous analytic estimation by an order of magnitude.

AI.tldr: This paper uses fully nonlinear numerical relativity to study PBH formation in an early matter-dominated era, comparing dust fluid and collisionless particle descriptions; it finds the black hole formation threshold is ~2× higher for dust (due to numerical singularities) and ~10× lower for particles than prior analytic estimates.
AI.motivation: To resolve discrepancies between analytic threshold estimates for primordial black hole (PBH) formation and numerical simulations, particularly under realistic early-universe matter descriptions and non-spherical (triaxial) initial perturbations.
AI.method: Fully nonlinear numerical relativity simulations with triaxial initial curvature perturbations (including ellipticity); two matter models: perfect dust fluid and collisionless N-body particle system; analysis of apparent horizon formation and numerical stability near density singularities.
AI.result: For dust fluid, simulations crash unless the singularity is hidden inside the apparent horizon, requiring initial amplitude >2× analytic threshold to observe horizon formation; for collisionless particles, no crash occurs, and PBH formation is observed at amplitudes ~10× smaller than the analytic threshold.
AI.conclusion: The PBH formation threshold is highly sensitive to the microphysical description of matter: analytic estimates assuming perfect fluid overpredict the threshold by up to an order of magnitude when kinetic (particle) effects dominate, implying previous constraints on PBH abundance may need revision.

title: Perturbations and quasinormal modes of black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
summary: We investigate the quasinormal spectra and time-domain evolution of scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations of the Einstein-Bronnikov black hole in Einstein gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics. The effective potentials associated with all perturbation sectors are shown to form positive potential barriers that vanish at the event horizon and spatial infinity. Their height increases with the magnetic charge, while the scalar perturbation possesses the largest potential barrier.
