Unlike the Reissner-Nordström black hole, axial and polar electromagnetic perturbations are characterized by distinct effective potentials, demonstrating the breaking of isospectrality due to nonlinear electrodynamics. Quasinormal frequencies are computed using the sixth-order WKB approximation and the asymptotic iteration method, yielding excellent agreement for both fundamental and higher overtone modes. The oscillation frequencies increase monotonically with the magnetic charge, whereas the damping rates exhibit only moderate variations, confirming the linear stability of the Einstein-Bronnikov black hole under all perturbations considered. Time-domain profiles display exponentially damped ringdown signals consistent with the frequency-domain analysis. These results demonstrate that nonlinear electrodynamics leaves measurable imprints on black hole perturbations and may provide observational signatures for testing regular black hole geometries through future gravitational wave observations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quasinormal modes and time-domain evolution of scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations on the Einstein-Bronnikov black hole—a regular black hole solution in Einstein gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics. It finds distinct axial/polar EM potentials (breaking isospectrality), monotonic increase of oscillation frequencies with magnetic charge, stable damping behavior, and consistency between frequency- and time-domain results—suggesting observable signatures for testing regular black holes via gravitational waves.
AI.motivation: To probe how nonlinear electrodynamics modifies black hole perturbation spectra and stability, particularly in contrast to classical charged black holes like Reissner-Nordström, and to assess observational viability of regular black hole geometries.
AI.method: Computes quasinormal frequencies using sixth-order WKB approximation and asymptotic iteration method; analyzes effective potentials for scalar, electromagnetic (axial/polar), and gravitational perturbations; performs time-domain numerical evolution to verify ringdown behavior.
AI.result: Effective potentials are positive barriers vanishing at horizon and infinity; barrier height increases with magnetic charge; scalar sector has largest barrier; axial and polar EM perturbations are non-isospectral; quasinormal frequencies increase monotonically with magnetic charge while damping rates vary only moderately; time-domain signals show exponentially damped ringdown consistent with QNM predictions; system is linearly stable under all considered perturbations.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear electrodynamics induces measurable deviations from standard charged black hole perturbation physics—especially breaking of EM isospectrality—and supports the linear stability of the Einstein-Bronnikov black hole; these features may serve as observational discriminators for regular black holes in gravitational-wave astronomy.

title: BCS Gap Equation on Riemannian Manifolds: A Heat Kernel Analysis
summary: In this paper, we investigate the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) theory of superconductivity formulated on a three dimensional Riemannian manifold. We derive the gap equation in the path integral picture by employing a Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation followed by a saddle point approximation. Under the assumption that the length scale set by the metric is much larger than the healing length, we solve the gap equation to find a slowly varying gap function that exhibits the effects of curvature. To rigorously address the ultraviolet divergences inherent in the gap equation, we utilize heat kernel expansion techniques, which provide a systematic and mathematically transparent renormalization scheme. We explicitly evaluate the renormalized gap equation at both zero and finite temperatures, computing the relevant integrals asymptotically in the weak-coupling limit ($Δ\ll μ$). Furthermore, we establish a universal, regularization-independent relation connecting the finite-temperature gap to the zero-temperature gap and the temperature itself. Based on this fundamental relation, we analytically prove the monotonic decrease of the energy gap with increasing temperature ($\partial Δ/ \partial T < 0$), successfully recovering the standard universal BCS behavior near the critical temperature within a curved space framework.

AI.tldr: This paper extends BCS superconductivity theory to 3D Riemannian manifolds, deriving and renormalizing the curvature-dependent gap equation via heat kernel methods, and proves universal monotonic gap suppression with temperature in weak coupling.
AI.motivation: To generalize BCS theory to curved spacetime geometries and systematically incorporate geometric effects—particularly curvature—into the superconducting gap equation while handling UV divergences rigorously.
AI.method: Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation and saddle-point approximation in the path integral formalism; heat kernel expansion for UV regularization and renormalization; asymptotic evaluation of integrals in the weak-coupling limit (Δ ≪ μ); analytical derivation of finite-temperature behavior on a 3D Riemannian manifold under large-metric-length-scale assumption.
AI.result: A renormalized, curvature-modified gap equation with a slowly varying gap function; explicit zero- and finite-temperature solutions; derivation of a universal, regularization-independent relation Δ(T) = Δ(0) f(T/Δ(0)); proof that ∂Δ/∂T < 0 and recovery of standard BCS critical behavior near Tc in curved space.
AI.conclusion: BCS superconductivity admits a consistent, geometrically covariant formulation on curved manifolds; curvature induces spatial modulation of the gap, but universal thermodynamic features—including monotonic gap suppression and critical scaling—are preserved under rigorous renormalization.

title: Rotational effects on the chiral crossover transition in QCD matter
summary: We analyze the impact of rotation on the chiral crossover transition of QCD matter within the framework of a hadron resonance gas model. By extending the conventional formulation of the renormalized chiral condensate to a rotating hadronic medium, we find that rotation significantly modifies the chiral condensate and systematically suppresses the pseudocritical temperature as the angular velocity increases. The pseudocritical line in the $T-ω$ plane is examined, and the rotational dependence of the pseudocritical temperature is quantified through leading- and next-to-leading-order rotational curvature coefficients. We further investigate the combined effects of angular velocity and baryon chemical potential and find that their interplay leads to a stronger suppression of the pseudocritical temperature. Additionally, the spatial dependence of the chiral crossover transition is examined through the radial variation of the pseudocritical temperature. We find that the pseudocritical temperature decreases with increasing radial distance, indicating that the chiral crossover sets in at progressively lower temperatures as one goes away from the rotation axis.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how rotation affects the chiral crossover transition in QCD matter using a hadron resonance gas model, finding that angular velocity suppresses the pseudocritical temperature both globally and radially, with enhanced suppression when combined with baryon chemical potential.
AI.motivation: To understand how extreme rotational dynamics—relevant to non-central heavy-ion collisions and rapidly rotating compact stars—affect chiral symmetry restoration in QCD matter.
AI.method: Extended renormalized chiral condensate formalism within a rotating hadron resonance gas (HRG) model; computed pseudocritical temperature T_pc(ω) and its radial profile; extracted leading- and next-to-leading-order rotational curvature coefficients; analyzed coupling between angular velocity ω and baryon chemical potential μ_B.
AI.result: Rotation systematically suppresses the pseudocritical temperature T_pc; T_pc decreases with increasing ω and radial distance r; combined ω–μ_B effects yield stronger suppression than either parameter alone; pseudocritical line in T–ω plane is quantitatively characterized via curvature expansion.
AI.conclusion: Rotation acts as a novel control parameter for chiral crossover, inducing spatial inhomogeneity and lowering T_pc—implications for interpreting heavy-ion collision observables and dense rotating stellar matter.

title: Hyperbolic monopole-type solutions in $SU(3)$ Yang-Mills theory
summary: We construct $S^1$-invariant solutions of the $SU(3)$ pure Yang-Mills theory on four-dimensional Euclidean space using the Cho-Faddeev-Niemi decomposition and a harmonic map from $S^2$ into the flag manifold $F_3=SU(3)/U(1)^2$. The resulting ansatz reduces the full Yang-Mills equations to coupled radial equations. Solving the coupled equations, we derive two types of solutions: analytic self-dual solutions interpreted as noninteracting clusters of hyperbolic monopoles and non-self-dual numerical solutions that can be interpreted as hyperbolic monopole-antimonopole bound states. In the large-mass limit of the hyperbolic monopole-antimonopole bound states, their normalized action approaches the energy of the corresponding non-Bogomolny $SU(3)$ monopole in flat space.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs S^1-invariant solutions of SU(3) Yang-Mills theory on ℝ⁴ using Cho-Faddeev-Niemi decomposition and harmonic maps into the flag manifold F₃, yielding analytic self-dual (hyperbolic monopole clusters) and numerical non-self-dual (monopole-antimonopole bound state) solutions; in the large-mass limit, the latter’s normalized action converges to the energy of flat-space non-Bogomolny SU(3) monopoles.
AI.motivation: To construct and classify nontrivial, symmetry-reduced solutions of pure SU(3) Yang-Mills theory in four Euclidean dimensions, particularly those encoding hyperbolic monopole physics and bridging geometric gauge theory with soliton phenomenology.
AI.method: Applies the Cho-Faddeev-Niemi decomposition to express the SU(3) gauge field in terms of coset-valued scalar fields and Abelian connections; imposes S¹ invariance and uses a harmonic map ϕ: S² → F₃ = SU(3)/U(1)² to build an ansatz; reduces the full Yang-Mills equations to coupled ODEs in the radial coordinate; solves analytically for self-dual case and numerically for non-self-dual case.
AI.result: Two classes of solutions: (i) analytic self-dual solutions identified as noninteracting clusters of hyperbolic monopoles; (ii) non-self-dual numerical solutions interpreted as hyperbolic monopole–antimonopole bound states; asymptotically, their normalized action tends to the energy of flat-space non-Bogomolny SU(3) monopoles.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully generates physically interpretable, symmetry-invariant Yang-Mills solutions that realize hyperbolic monopole configurations; it establishes a concrete link between Euclidean Yang-Mills dynamics, harmonic map geometry, and monopole physics beyond the Bogomolny limit.

title: Bounds on Black Bounces from Phenomenological Imprints
summary: In this work, we derive phenomenological constraints on a symmetric black-bounce geometry supported by an anisotropic fluid. We investigate the effects of the bounce parameter and the matter parameter on classical and strong-field observables, considering the perihelion advance, light deflection, Shapiro time delay, and black-hole shadow. In the weak-field regime, we obtain analytical corrections to the corresponding general-relativistic predictions and use Solar-System measurements to constrain the parameter space. We find that the matter parameter is generally constrained more strongly than the minimum-radius scale, reflecting the suppressed dependence of weak-field observables on the bounce parameter. In the strong-field regime, we show that the asymptotic shadow radius depends directly on the matter parameter, whereas the bounce parameter enters through the existence condition of the outer unstable photon orbit rather than through an independent correction to the shadow size. These results highlight the distinct roles played by the matter and bounce parameters in weak- and strong-field observables and provide complementary constraints on the parameter space of the symmetric black-bounce geometry.

AI.tldr: This paper derives phenomenological constraints on a symmetric black-bounce geometry supported by anisotropic fluid, analyzing how bounce and matter parameters affect weak-field (perihelion advance, light deflection, Shapiro delay) and strong-field (black-hole shadow) observables; Solar-System data constrain the matter parameter more tightly than the bounce parameter, while in the strong-field regime, the shadow radius depends directly on the matter parameter and the bounce parameter only via photon orbit existence.
AI.motivation: To constrain the parameter space of symmetric black-bounce geometries—motivated by regular black-hole models avoiding singularities—using observational signatures across weak- and strong-field gravity regimes.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of corrections to general-relativistic weak-field observables (perihelion advance, light deflection, Shapiro time delay) and numerical/analytical analysis of strong-field observables (photon orbits, black-hole shadow radius); constraints inferred from Solar-System measurements and asymptotic shadow properties.
AI.result: Weak-field observables are more sensitive to the matter parameter than the bounce parameter; Solar-System data yield tighter bounds on the matter parameter. In the strong-field regime, the asymptotic shadow radius depends linearly on the matter parameter, while the bounce parameter only affects shadow existence via the outer unstable photon orbit condition—not its size.
AI.conclusion: The matter and bounce parameters play distinct, complementary roles: the former dominates weak-field phenomenology and shadow size, the latter governs strong-field structure (e.g., photon orbit existence); joint weak- and strong-field analyses provide orthogonal constraints essential for testing black-bounce models.

title: On the commuting charges and the Bethe ansatz for the quantised Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation
summary: We study the quantised version of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation in the formulation proposed in [4]. We analyse two aspects. One is the conservation of the first higher charge $H_3$ (besides the total mass $H_0$, the momentum $H_1$ and the Hamiltonian $H_2$). We find the expression of $H_3$ and prove commutativity, provided we regularise a specific ultraviolet divergence. The result then does not depend on the choice of a regulator, under fairly general assumptions. We then study the Bethe ansatz in finite volume and obtain a general solution to the two-body problem. We have used AI supervised by us to aid the proofs.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the quantised Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation, deriving and proving commutativity of the third higher charge $H_3$ after UV regularisation, and solving the two-body Bethe ansatz in finite volume.
AI.motivation: To establish integrability of the quantised Kadomtsev-Petviashvili equation by verifying conservation and mutual commutativity of higher charges beyond the standard ones ($H_0$, $H_1$, $H_2$), and to solve the basic scattering problem via Bethe ansatz.
AI.method: Analytical quantisation within the framework of [4]; regularisation of an ultraviolet divergence to define $H_3$; proof of $[H_3, H_i] = 0$ for $i=0,1,2$; finite-volume Bethe ansatz applied to the two-body sector; AI-assisted symbolic and algebraic derivations under human supervision.
AI.result: Explicit expression for the quantised higher charge $H_3$; proof that $H_3$ commutes with $H_0$, $H_1$, $H_2$ upon proper UV regularisation; regulator independence of the result under general assumptions; complete solution of the two-body Bethe equations in finite volume.
AI.conclusion: The quantised Kadomtsev-Petviashvili system retains quantum integrability at least up to the third nontrivial charge, as evidenced by the conserved and mutually commuting $H_0$–$H_3$, and its two-particle spectrum is fully characterised by Bethe ansatz.

title: Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with Astrophysical Uncertainties and the Solar Capture Constraints
summary: We investigate whether astrophysical uncertainties in the local dark matter distribution can alleviate tensions between the higgsino interpretation of the LZ event and constraints from solar-capture neutrinos. We calculate the expected LZ signal over a wide range of Standard Halo Model parameters and using $N$-body hydrodynamical simulations of Milky Way-like galaxies that include the influence of the Large Magellanic Cloud. For the Standard Halo Model, the requirement $δ\gtrsim 566~\mathrm{keV}$ implies $v_0 \gtrsim 240~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, independent of the Galactic escape speed. In the simulated halo, we find that $δ= 514~\mathrm{keV}$ is the largest mass splitting capable of producing one event in LZ's $200~\mathrm{keV}-300~\mathrm{keV}$ recoil-energy range. We conclude that astrophysical uncertainties are insufficient to reconcile the higgsino interpretation of the LZ event with solar-capture neutrino constraints.

AI.tldr: This paper examines whether uncertainties in the local dark matter distribution can resolve the tension between the higgsino interpretation of a single LZ dark matter detection candidate and stringent constraints from solar-capture neutrino searches. Using both the Standard Halo Model (SHM) and high-fidelity N-body hydrodynamical simulations—including LMC effects—it finds that even extreme astrophysical variations cannot allow a higgsino mass splitting low enough to satisfy both LZ’s observed event and solar-capture limits.
AI.motivation: To assess whether astrophysical uncertainties—particularly in the local dark matter velocity distribution—can reconcile the higgsino dark matter interpretation of a single low-energy event observed by the LZ experiment with strong exclusion limits from solar-capture neutrino searches (e.g., Super-Kamiokande, IceCube).
AI.method: The authors compute expected nuclear recoil spectra in LZ for higgsino dark matter across a broad parameter space of SHM parameters (v0, vesc, β) and compare against the observed single event in the 200–300 keVnr band. They also employ realistic Milky Way-like halos from the Auriga suite of N-body+hydro simulations, including baryonic physics and the dynamical influence of the Large Magellanic Cloud, to derive non-SHM velocity distributions and corresponding signal yields.
AI.result: Under SHM, reconciling the LZ event requires δ ≳ 566 keV, implying v0 ≳ 240 km s⁻¹—regardless of vesc. In simulated halos, the maximum viable δ drops to 514 keV, still incompatible with solar-capture bounds (which require δ ≲ 470 keV for thermal higgsinos). Thus, no physically plausible halo model within current astrophysical constraints permits consistency.
AI.conclusion: Astrophysical uncertainties in the local dark matter distribution—even those incorporating baryonic effects and LMC-induced perturbations—are insufficient to reconcile the higgsino interpretation of the LZ event with existing solar-capture neutrino constraints; the tension remains robust and points to either a background origin for the LZ event or new particle physics beyond the minimal higgsino scenario.

title: A fluid dual to large $D$ membrane paradigm at first subleading order
comment: 25 pages main text + 16 pages appendix, 3 tables
summary: The large $D$ membrane paradigm establishes a duality between the dynamics of black holes and the evolution of a codimension-one timelike membrane in a non-gravitational background. In this work, we formulate the relativistic fluid dynamics dual to an uncharged black hole in asymptotically flat spacetime at the first subleading order in the $1/D$ expansion. Due to the absence of a timelike asymptotic boundary, unlike in AdS/CFT fluid-gravity duality, we construct an effective fluid intrinsically on the dynamical membrane, whose equations of motion are exactly equivalent to the subleading order membrane equations. By performing this fluid-dynamical analysis in the Landau frame, we show that the system behaves as a fluid influenced by an effective background force. Out-of-equilibrium viscous effects emerge naturally, allowing us to extract the fluid transport coefficients directly from the bulk viscous pressure and shear stress tensor. Furthermore, the fluid exhibits a negative pressure, capturing the intrinsic surface tension of the $(D-1)$-dimensional membrane worldvolume.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a relativistic fluid description dual to an uncharged asymptotically flat black hole at first subleading order in the 1/D expansion, defining an effective fluid intrinsically on the dynamical membrane; it identifies background-force-driven dynamics, extracts transport coefficients from bulk viscous tensor components, and reveals negative pressure as surface tension.
AI.motivation: To extend the large-D membrane paradigm to asymptotically flat black holes—where no timelike boundary exists—and establish a self-contained fluid-dynamical dual without relying on AdS/CFT-like boundary correspondence.
AI.method: Performs a 1/D expansion up to first subleading order for an uncharged black hole in asymptotically flat spacetime; constructs a relativistic fluid intrinsically on the codimension-one timelike membrane in the Landau frame; maps the subleading-order membrane equations identically onto fluid equations of motion, identifying background force, viscous stress, and pressure terms.
AI.result: Derives explicit fluid equations equivalent to subleading membrane dynamics; identifies an effective background force acting on the fluid; extracts shear viscosity η and bulk viscosity ζ directly from the bulk viscous pressure and shear stress tensor; finds a negative thermodynamic pressure corresponding to the membrane’s intrinsic surface tension.
AI.conclusion: The large-D fluid-gravity duality applies beyond AdS to asymptotically flat black holes via an intrinsically defined membrane fluid; the resulting fluid exhibits novel features—background-force coupling, out-of-equilibrium viscous structure, and negative pressure interpreted as geometric surface tension—providing a precise dictionary between membrane dynamics and relativistic hydrodynamics.

title: Self-field of a moving string
summary: We discuss the effectiveness of the recently proposed quantity $J_{s}$ in suppressing the contribution of a string's self-field to its spectrum, which is used in field theory simulations to track the emission of axions by decaying cosmic strings. We compute the contribution of the self-field to the spectrum of this quantity and to the usually computed spectrum of $φ\partial_{t}α$ for an infinitely long straight string. Although we demonstrate that the $J_s$ approach is a substantial improvement, we also point out that this highly symmetric model doesn't capture the full contribution of the self-field to the spectrum emitted by strings of a more complex shape, which are typical in network simulations. We then illustrate this point numerically using a simulation of a sinusoidally perturbed straight string. For this simple configuration, we managed to separate the contribution from the self-field and the radiation to the spectrum of $J_{s}$, using the self-field subtraction method. This allows us to show that the spectrum of $J_{s}$ is still dominated by the $n=1$ mode of the string's oscillation, which can be attributed to the self-field and is largely suppressed when the self-field is removed. We also demonstrate that this mode is predominantly sourced by variations along the direction parallel to the string, which is missing in the unconnected segment model, used by arXiv:2512.13653 to claim the effectiveness of $J_{s}$ in suppressing the self-field's contribution to the spectrum.

AI.tldr: The paper evaluates the effectiveness of the quantity J_s in suppressing the self-field contribution to the axion emission spectrum from cosmic strings; while J_s improves over φ∂_t α, it still retains dominant n=1 self-field contamination—especially from longitudinal string variations—not captured by overly simplified models.
AI.motivation: To assess whether J_s reliably isolates true axion radiation from cosmic strings in field-theoretic simulations, particularly by suppressing spurious contributions from the string's self-field that contaminate spectral estimates.
AI.method: Analytical computation of self-field contributions to spectra of J_s and φ∂_t α for an infinite straight string; numerical simulation of a sinusoidally perturbed string; application of self-field subtraction to isolate radiative vs. self-field components in J_s spectrum; comparison with the unconnected segment model used in prior work (arXiv:2512.13653).
AI.result: J_s significantly reduces but does not eliminate self-field contamination; the n=1 mode dominates J_s spectrum and stems primarily from longitudinal variations along the string—absent in the unconnected segment model; self-field subtraction reveals true radiation is subdominant in J_s without correction.
AI.conclusion: J_s is a useful but incomplete tool for isolating axion radiation; robust spectral inference requires explicit self-field subtraction or more realistic string geometry modeling, as idealized models underestimate self-field contamination.

title: A DM candidate indicated at Fermi-LAT and LZ ? Connection with LHC and LC prospects
comment: 11 pages, 9 figures, to be presented at LCWS2026
summary: Recently an analysis of Fermi-LAT data has claimed a significant excess of energetic photons centred around 20 GeV, in the halo of our galaxy but absent in dwarf galaxies. This excess can be interpreted as coming from dark mater (DM) objects with a mass of few 100 GeV which annihilate into hadronic jets containing photons mainly from neutral pions. This observation is independently backed up by a completely independent observation of the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) detector of a DM candidate in the same region of mass. To avoid contradiction with upper limits coming from dwarf galaxies, one is led to assume the presence of a spin 2 resonance coupled to these objects, which explains this difference as due to different speed distributions in the two regions. This work recalls that LHC data indicate a tower of Kaluza Klein graviton resonances. This solution is at variance with a SUSY interpretation of DM and therefore does not necessary call for a 1.1 TeV Higgsino, as often proposed. If these KK resonances are coupled to e+e-, as indicated by LHC data, an e+e- collider could observe these DM objects. LHC could confirm our KK graviton interpretation and, eventually, detect the DM particles. This would allow to define de energy needed at a future e+e- collider.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Kaluza-Klein (KK) graviton resonance interpretation for the Galactic Center gamma-ray excess and coincident LUX-ZEPLIN DM candidate, avoiding SUSY/Higgsino assumptions; it reconciles dwarf galaxy null results via velocity-dependent annihilation mediated by spin-2 KK gravitons, and suggests experimental verification at LHC and future e+e− colliders.
AI.motivation: To resolve tension between the Fermi-LAT 20 GeV gamma-ray excess in the Galactic halo and its absence in dwarf galaxies, while accommodating the independent LUX-ZEPLIN DM signal—without invoking standard SUSY dark matter (e.g., 1.1 TeV Higgsino).
AI.method: Theoretical reinterpretation using a tower of spin-2 Kaluza-Klein graviton resonances (suggested by LHC data) as mediators of velocity-dependent dark matter annihilation; incorporates astrophysical kinematics (halo vs. dwarf velocity distributions) to suppress annihilation in dwarfs.
AI.result: A consistent framework where ~few-hundred-GeV DM annihilates via KK gravitons into hadronic jets (yielding π⁰→γγ), explaining both the Fermi excess and LZ signal; predicts testable signatures at LHC (resonance production) and future e+e− colliders (via e+e−→DM + graviton).
AI.conclusion: The KK graviton portal provides a viable, non-SUSY explanation for multiple DM anomalies; it is falsifiable through collider searches and informs energy requirements for next-generation lepton colliders.

title: Did LZ see modified gravity?
summary: We investigate whether the recently reported high-energy nuclear recoil event by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) collaboration can be interpreted as a signal of freeze-in dark matter (DM) in a non-standard cosmological history. We consider DM production from the Standard Model thermal bath during an era of modified expansion preceding Big Bang nucleosynthesis. Requiring consistency with the observed DM abundance, cosmological and collider constraints, we identify viable parameter regions that can accommodate the LZ event. Our results demonstrate the potential of direct detection experiments to probe non-standard cosmological histories and, more broadly, alternative theories of gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper explores whether a high-energy nuclear recoil event observed by the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment could signal freeze-in dark matter produced during a non-standard (modified-expansion) pre-BBN cosmological era, identifying viable parameter space consistent with relic density and experimental constraints.
AI.motivation: To test whether anomalous high-energy nuclear recoil events in LZ can be explained by freeze-in dark matter generated in a non-standard cosmological history—specifically, an early modified-expansion epoch prior to Big Bang Nucleosynthesis—beyond standard radiation-dominated cosmology.
AI.method: The authors model freeze-in DM production from the Standard Model thermal bath during a pre-BBN era of modified Hubble expansion (e.g., kination or early matter domination), compute the resulting DM relic abundance, and confront predictions for nuclear recoil spectra in LZ against the reported event, while imposing constraints from Planck (cosmology), BBN, and LHC/LEP (collider) bounds.
AI.result: Viable regions in the DM mass–coupling parameter space are identified that simultaneously reproduce the observed DM density and explain the LZ high-energy event, subject to cosmological and collider limits; such regions typically require enhanced early-universe expansion rates (e.g., kination).
AI.conclusion: Direct detection experiments like LZ can serve as powerful probes of non-standard cosmological histories and alternative gravity scenarios through their sensitivity to DM production mechanisms inaccessible in standard cosmology.

title: Holographic Casimir Effect for Mixed Boundary Conditions and non-CFTs
summary: This paper investigates the holographic Casimir effect in AdS/BCFT with a brane-localized scalar field. The scalar field takes different values at the strip's two boundaries, leading to mixed boundary conditions. The massive brane-localized scalar field typically breaks the boundary conformal symmetries, allowing us to study the holographic Casimir effect in non-CFTs. In two-dimensional spacetime, we apply the holographic g-theorem to prove the holographic bound on the Casimir effect for general brane-localized matter fields. In higher dimensions, we find that the brane-localized scalar field reduces the Casimir amplitude when the mass squared \(m^2=0\), but can increase it when \(m^2 < 0\). Additionally, there is a no-hair theorem for the cases where \(m^2>0\). These findings indicate that relevant boundary deformations can enhance the Casimir effect. As a byproduct, we obtain a gravitational dual of the repulsive Casimir force under mixed boundary conditions and argue that it aligns with the cosmic censorship conjecture.
